assumptions: The court image content id is not recorded; the image name is a declared venue, not a verified identity.
The CPU microcode revision is not recorded; only the model and the flag set are.
A component with digest UNKNOWN participates in the TCB digest by its recorded version string and check state, not by bytes.

check.mechanism: `ar --version` plus sha256 of the resolved binary

components.could_invalidate: The crate archive is produced by ar; a different ar changes member order, metadata and the archive digest.
components.name: GNU ar

check.mechanism: `as --version` plus sha256 of the resolved binary

components.could_invalidate: Inline assembly and compiler-emitted assembly are encoded by as; a different assembler can encode a different instruction.
components.name: GNU assembler

check.mechanism: `cargo -V` plus sha256 of the resolved binary

components.could_invalidate: cargo resolves features, profiles and build scripts; a different cargo can select different inputs.
components.name: cargo

check.mechanism: `cc --version` plus sha256 of the resolved binary

components.could_invalidate: The distribution DSO is linked by cc; its driver decides startup objects, PIE and linker flags.
components.name: C compiler driver used for the distribution link and harnesses

check.evidence: image name recorded; content id not obtained
check.mechanism: NONE: the container cannot inspect its own image identity without host access

components.could_invalidate: A different image changes every tool and library in this table at once.

digest.method: obtain on the host with `docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' openssl-rs-court-tools:1`

components.name: Court container image

check.mechanism: read /proc/cpuinfo

components.could_invalidate: A different CPU or microarchitecture can execute the same instruction stream with different timing and different feature availability.
components.name: CPU that executes the artefact

check.evidence: runtime sites=[]; cfg(target_arch) sites=20; explicit flags=[]
check.mechanism: scan src/**.rs for is_x86_feature_detected/is_aarch64_feature_detected, count cfg(target_arch = "x86_64"), and scan Cargo.toml/rust-toolchain.toml/.cargo/config.toml for target-cpu/target-feature

components.could_invalidate: A runtime feature test or an explicit target-cpu/target-feature can select different code than the audited baseline.

digest.method: a dispatch mechanism has no file digest; its identity is the source scan plus the target flags

components.version: compile-time cfg(target_arch) selection; 0 runtime feature-detection site(s)

check.mechanism: readlink of /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 plus sha256

components.version: UNKNOWN: the loader has no version command

check.mechanism: `uname -r`

components.could_invalidate: The kernel supplies the loader interface, scheduling and the timestamp counter; a different kernel changes the venue.

components.name: Linux kernel

check.mechanism: `ld --version` plus sha256 of the resolved binary

components.could_invalidate: The linker lays out sections and resolves symbol versions; a different linker changes the artefact digest and can change indirect-call resolution.
components.name: GNU ld

check.mechanism: `ldd --version` plus sha256 of the resolved libc

components.could_invalidate: libc supplies allocation, I/O, threading and the process start state; a different libc changes runtime behaviour even for the same DSO bytes.
components.name: GNU C library

check.mechanism: sha256 of the resolved libgcc_s

components.could_invalidate: The unwinder is the panic boundary's runtime dependency; a different unwinder changes what happens between a panic and the FFI guard.

components.version: UNKNOWN: libgcc_s has no version command

check.mechanism: `rustc -vV` for the version; sha256 of the resolved libLLVM

components.could_invalidate: LLVM lowering, scheduling and inlining decide the emitted instruction shape; an LLVM change can add a branch or remove a cmov.

check.mechanism: `objdump --version` plus sha256 of the resolved binary

components.could_invalidate: The branch audit sees instructions only through objdump; a different decoder can change the counted branches and cmovs.
components.name: GNU objdump, used by the branch audit

check.mechanism: read the release profile and scan src/ffi/mod.rs for guard_ffi/catch_unwind

components.could_invalidate: A profile change from unwind to abort, or a weakened guard, makes the documented failure value unreachable.

digest.method: the boundary is repository source (`src/ffi/mod.rs`), not a third-party artefact; its consuming runtime is recorded above

components.name: guard_ffi unwind boundary

components.could_invalidate: The panic strategy and unwinder back `guard_ffi`; a different runtime changes whether a panic is caught or aborts.
